Differences

Why A-Levels Are Academically Different

What changes between GCSE and A-Level, and why preparation matters.

01

Sharper Content

A-Level Mathematics introduces calculus, never seen at GCSE, used through university.

02

Independent Thought

Schools typically pair one taught period with two hours of independent study.

03

Longer Answers

A-Level History essays run around 800 words; English Literature responses 1,200 words.

04

Subject Focus

Students pick three or four subjects and study them in much greater depth than at GCSE.

From Knowledge to Analysis

A-Level study asks more of your child than GCSE ever did.

Applying Knowledge

Familiar ideas now appear in questions your child has never seen before.

Connecting Topics

Topics no longer sit alone; they must link across the whole syllabus.

Evaluating Evidence

Sources, claims, and answers all need to hold up under clear reasoning.

Independent Thinking

Marks come from analysis and judgement, not from cramming the night before.

Building Independent Academic Thinking

What A-Level study looks like outside lessons, and where Ustaad steadies the work.

01

Self-Direction

Revision becomes your child's job at Year 12; Ustaad keeps the work from drifting.

02

Sound Judgement

Each week your child must pick what to study next; we guide that choice.

03

Layered Problems

Compound problems need a written plan first; tutors coach that habit until it sticks.

04

Workload Habits

Three A-Levels need five to six hours each week; we keep schedules on track.

The Ustaad Approach to A-Level Excellence

Four ways Ustaad supports students through the two A-Level years.

Address Gaps Early

Year 11 trigonometry gaps surface in Year 12 Mechanics within the first half-term.

Joining Topics

Tutors help students connect ideas across the syllabus, which higher-mark questions reward.

Sharper Writing

Essays and longer answers sharpen through drafting, marking, and feedback.

Two-Year Rhythm

Year 12 mocks in May, Year 13 mocks in November, final papers from May.

University Pathways

University Pathways and Competitive Admissions

How A-Level choices shape university access and competitive degree applications.

Every offer letter turns on two things: A-Level grades and the subjects behind them.

Medicine, engineering, and law each set their own non-negotiable subject combinations and minimum grades.

Ustaad guides A-Level choices in Year 11 and protects each predicted grade through finals.

A-Level study unfolds over two demanding years, during which UAE families often balance final-year preparation with university applications, predicted grades, and entrance test windows. Whether a student attends a British system school in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah, or Fujairah, the A-Level path runs in parallel with the wider admissions cycle. Ustaad's A-Level tutors work alongside students through both Year 12 and Year 13, holding subject understanding steady from first-year topics through to final-year synoptic papers, while parents and schools focus on the larger university plan.
